title: Agentic AI is advancing faster than enterprises can absorb it

content_html:
Hillary Remy

Tue, August 11, 2026 at 4:37 PM PDT 6 min read

Agentic AI is everywhere in the enterprise conversation right now. Vendors are promising systems that do not just assist humans but execute decisions, manage workflows, and coordinate transactions across entire organizations without being asked. The pitch is compelling. The reality is considerably more complicated.

The gap between where agentic AI is being sold and where it is actually being deployed is one of the defining tensions in enterprise technology in 2026. And it is wider than most buyers realize.

Why B2B is harder than it looks for AI agents

Consumer AI applications have a relatively simple job. They deal with individual users, standard interfaces, and relatively predictable inputs. B2B commerce is a different environment entirely.

Pricing is often negotiated customer by customer. Workflows vary across business units and geographies. Approvals span multiple layers of decision-makers who each have different authority levels. Supply chains involve dozens of third-party systems that were not designed to talk to each other, let alone to an AI agent trying to coordinate across all of them simultaneously.

"B2B leaders are hungry for AI, but they're not looking to hand over all the keys just yet," Jary Carter, co-founder and CRO of OroCommerce, told TheStreet. "When you dig into their real-world operations, the demand isn't for complete autonomy. Most of them want AI to make their people faster and smarter, not to replace the judgment calls that define how they do business." Carter has spent more than a decade building enterprise commerce software for manufacturers, distributors, and wholesalers, and his company works with organizations ranging from mid-market to Fortune 500 scale.

In B2B commerce, the relationship between buyer and seller is often the product itself. A longtime purchasing manager at a regional distributor does not just want the right price, they want to know someone is paying attention to their account. Delegating that to a system that operates probabilistically, without human accountability, is a risk many B2B leaders are not willing to take. At least not yet.

"The concern I hear most often is not 'can AI do this?' — it is 'what happens if AI is wrong?'" Carter said. "B2B retention is built on trust, and trust is built on accuracy."

The infrastructure gap nobody is talking about

Much of the excitement around agentic AI assumes enterprises are ready to plug intelligent systems into clean, standardized environments. They are not.

content_html_zh:
希拉里·雷米

太平洋夏令时间 2026 年 8 月 11 日星期二下午 4:37 阅读 6 分钟

目前，代理人工智能在企业对话中无处不在。 供应商是有前途的系统，它们不仅可以帮助人类，还可以在未经询问的情况下执行决策、管理工作流程并协调整个组织的事务。 球场很引人注目。 现实要复杂得多。

代理人工智能的销售地点与实际部署地点之间的差距是 2026 年企业技术的决定性紧张之一。 而且它比大多数买家意识到的更广泛。

为什么 B2B 比寻找 AI 代理更难

消费者人工智能应用程序的工作相对简单。 它们处理个人用户、标准接口和相对可预测的输入。 B2B 商务是一个完全不同的环境。

定价通常是由客户与客户协商确定的。 工作流程因业务部门和地区的不同而有所不同。 批准跨越多层决策者，每个决策者都有不同的权限级别。 供应链涉及数十个第三方系统，这些系统的设计初衷并不是为了相互通信，更不用说与试图同时协调​​所有这些系统的人工智能代理了。

OroCommerce 联合创始人兼 CRO Jary Carter 告诉 TheStreet：“B2B 领导者渴望人工智能，但他们还不打算交出所有钥匙。” “当你深入研究他们的现实世界运营时，你会发现他们的需求并不是完全自主。 他们中的大多数人希望人工智能让他们的员工更快、更聪明，而不是取代定义他们如何开展业务的判断力。” Carter 花了十多年的时间为制造商、分销商和批发商构建企业商务软件，他的公司与从中端市场到财富 500 强规模的组织合作。

更多人工智能：

  • 英伟达刚刚采取了华尔街尚未准备好的举措
  • 微软刚刚在人工智能政策斗争中选边站
  • OpenAI 刚刚披露了一些真正令人震惊的事情

在 B2B 商务中，买方和卖方之间的关系通常是产品本身。 区域经销商的长期采购经理不仅仅想要合适的价格，他们还想知道有人正在关注他们的帐户。 将其委托给一个按概率运行且没有人为责任的系统是许多 B2B 领导者不愿意承担的风险。 至少现在还没有。

“我最常听到的担忧不是‘人工智能能做到这一点吗？’ ——问题是‘如果人工智能出错了怎么办？’”卡特说。 “B2B 保留建立在信任的基础上，而信任则建立在准确性的基础上。”

无人谈论的基础设施差距

围绕代理人工智能的许多令人兴奋的事情都假设企业已准备好将智能系统插入到干净、标准化的环境中。 他们不是。
